title: Decision trees compare caregiver ratings with clinical ADHD diagnoses
summary: In 326 Italian children and adolescents referred for suspected ADHD, a decision tree using caregiver questionnaires agreed with clinician diagnoses in 74% of leave-one-out evaluations. Analysis of fitted-model errors linked autism-related symptom ratings to classification patterns. This is a retrospective comparison with clinical assessments, not an independently validated remote diagnostic service. Shared questionnaire information, a selected mostly male sample and exploratory error analysis limit interpretation.
ai_technology: Decision tree; random forest and support-vector-machine comparisons

source_review.scope: Primary relevant participant/reference, questionnaire, tree/LOO Methods, Results and limitations. Supplementary data-cleaning appendix not inspected. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Among 342 referred children, sixteen with extensive missing data were excluded, leaving 326. A decision tree was evaluated against DSM-5-based clinician assessments using leave-one-out validation; accuracy was 74%, sensitivity 92% and specificity 50%. Separate error-pattern analyses used fitted full-sample predictions.
evidence.unknown: Generalization to other referral populations, independent diagnostic reference assessment and prospective telehealth effectiveness remain unestablished. The clinicians’ diagnostic process incorporated caregiver information also available to the algorithm; exploratory autism/error associations do not establish causal confounding or independently validated subgroup performance. Supplementary data-cleaning details were not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: The tree learns questionnaire-score splits that classify clinician-assessed ADHD status; learned classifications and their errors support analysis of which reported symptom patterns depart from the full in-person evaluation.
